subject: Region pinning / data residency follow-up (Orion Bank)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Tom Brewer <tbrewer@orionbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T14:05:00Z
Subject: Region pinning / data residency (post-call recap)

Hi Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups from our discovery call:

- Summary: Orion needs production traffic and data residency constrained to EU regions (EU-only for PII). Development/non-prod may be allowed in US but must be clearly separated.
- Requirements you called out:
  - PII must never leave EU for production workloads
  - Backups and snapshots must be stored in EU; retention policy to be defined (you mentioned 7 years as a hard requirement for audit data)
  - Audit/logging: detailed per-request logs, immutable audit trail, and exportable logs for your SIEM
  - Key management: customer-managed KMS preferred; HSM option for Private deployments
  - Failover: you want cross-region failover for DR but only to be used under explicit conditions — need to understand acceptable RTO/RPO and whether failover to non-EU is allowed in emergency

Next steps I propose:
1) Can you confirm whether the 7-year retention applies to all request logs or only certain audit artifacts?
2) If cross-region failover is allowed for DR, is failover to US acceptable as long as data is encrypted in transit and at rest?
3) I’ll loop in Aditya (solutions) for a technical deep-dive on how region pinning and failover behave at runtime, and Marissa to align commercial/contractual constraints.

I’ve attached a short design sketch that shows how we typically implement region pinning and backup controls.

Best,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com

From: Tom Brewer <tbrewer@orionbank.com>

Cc: Orion Bank Security <security@orionbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-03T18:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Region pinning / data residency (post-call recap)

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the succinct recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Retention: The 7-year retention is mandatory for transaction audit logs and PII-related artifacts for regulatory reasons. Other operational logs (metrics, standard access logs) can be shorter (90 days) if needed.
- Failover: We are open to a cross-region failover model under strict controls:
  - Primary: EU (Frankfurt)
  - Secondary: US (east) only for full DR events where we have declared a disaster and have explicit approval from our compliance team
  - For failover to US we need assurances that backups/snapshots containing PII remain encrypted with keys we control and that cross-border transfer is logged and auditable
- KMS: Customer-managed keys are required for prod. We will need details on KMS integrations (AWS KMS / CloudHSM equivalents) and any key usage logs available.
- Audit logs: We need immutability guarantees and the ability to export logs to our Splunk/SIEM.

If you can confirm those points and share the compliance pack and architecture doc, we’ll pick a date next week for the deep-dive with our infra and security SMEs.

Regards,
Tom Brewer
Head of Cloud Security | Orion Bank
tbrewer@orionbank.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Tom Brewer <tbrewer@orionbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Orion Bank Security <security@orionbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-04T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Region pinning / data residency (post-call recap)

Tom —

Appreciate the clarity. Short answers up front and then proposed next steps:

- Retention: We can support 7-year retention for transaction audit logs and any PII-associated artifacts. That’s typically handled as a separate long-term archive tier (immutable snapshots). Operational logs default to 90 days; extended retention is available as an add-on.
- Failover: Our platform supports region pinning (route-by-policy) so production traffic can be enforced to EU endpoints. Cross-region failover is supported but treated as an explicit policy — it can be configured to require a manual trigger or an approval workflow.
  - Failover behavior: failover is asynchronous — we recommend a warm-standby in secondary region to meet your RTO/RPO targets.
  - Cross-border data movement: We can restrict backups and long-term archives to EU-only unless you opt-in for cross-region replication; any cross-region transfer will be logged and surfaced in audit logs.
- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault/GCP KMS) and have an on-prem HSM integration for Private deployments. Keys can be imported or generated per-tenant; key usage logs are available and can be exported.
- Audit logs & exports: Immutable audit trail with signed log entries is supported. We can stream logs to your SIEM (S3 -> Splunk/HTTP) or provide daily exports. Retention and immutability options will be in the compliance pack.

I’ve attached the compliance pack and a more detailed architecture diagram (redwood-compliance-pack.zip, includes SOC2 summary, encryption details, and pattern for region pinning).

Next steps:
- Aditya, can you propose a 60-minute deep-dive (technical) where we walk through region pinning, backup snapshot flows, KMS integration, and failover runbook?
- Tom/Orion: if you can share preferred times next week and the security SMEs you want on the call, we’ll schedule.

Thanks —
Lauren

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Tom Brewer <tbrewer@orionbank.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Orion Bank Security <security@orionbank.com>

Subject: Re: Region pinning / data residency (post-call recap)

Hey Tom / team —

I’ll be the lead on the technical deep-dive. Quick technical notes so you have context before the call:

1) Region pinning model:
   - Tenant-level routing: we assign a tenant region tag; all production API endpoints will terminate in that region. DNS + edge routing ensures requests are served from EU endpoints.
   - KV / cache: model KV cache is local to the serving region; we replicate critical state to the warm-standby asynchronously to avoid latency impact on the primary writes.

2) Failover & DR:
   - Warm-standby approach recommended: replicate model weights, config, and essential state to secondary region on a schedule; KV cache is rebuilt on failover (expect initial latency as caches warm).
   - RTO/RPO: typical RTO for warm-standby is minutes to low tens of minutes depending on model size and KV rebuild; we’ll run a tabletop exercise to estimate for your workloads.

3) Backups & snapshots:
   - Snapshots of persistent stores are stored encrypted in the tenant-designated region (S3-like object store).
   - We can enable cross-region replication as an explicit opt-in. If cross-region replication is disabled, snapshots remain in EU only.

4) KMS/HSM:
   - Supports external KMS keys; we perform envelope encryption and never persist unencrypted keys.
   - Key usage and key rotation logs are available and can be exported to your audit store.

5) Audit logs:
   - We provide per-request metadata, identity context, and routing decisions. Logs are tamper-evident and can be exported to your SIEM in near real-time.

I’ll include a simple failover runbook and an example config that pins traffic to the eu-west-1 equivalent and shows a manual failover step. Proposed times for the deep-dive: 2026-08-06 14:00 UTC or 2026-08-07 09:00 UTC — let me know which works for you and we’ll share a calendar invite and a short pre-read.

—Aditya
